svg.aria-label: Decision tree distinguishing Capital Expenditure from Revenue Expenditure and showing profit distortion if misclassified
svg.text: Capital Expenditure vs. Revenue Expenditure Decision Tree
Ask ONE decisive test question before recording any business spending — getting it wrong distorts BOTH Profit and Assets!
DECISION TEST: Does this spending acquire, install, or PERMANENTLY
improve/extend the earning power of a Non-Current Asset (> 1 year)?
YES
NO
CAPITAL EXPENDITURE → Balance Sheet (NCA)
Long-term benefit (> 1 year) · Non-recurring
• Buying premises, delivery vans, machinery, computers
• Legal fees, stamp duty & delivery/installation of NEW asset
• Adding a brand-new warehouse wing or AC system
• Upgrading an old engine to double capacity/life
Misclassified as Revenue Expense?
Expenses TOO HIGH → Profit & Non-Current Assets UNDERSTATED!
REVENUE EXPENDITURE → Income Statement
Day-to-day running & maintenance (< 1 year) · Recurring
• Buying goods for resale (Purchases) & staff wages
• Petrol/fuel, road license & annual van insurance
• Repainting existing walls or replacing broken glass/tires
• Servicing & repairs that merely RESTORE normal condition
Misclassified as Capital Asset?
Expenses TOO LOW → Profit & Non-Current Assets OVERSTATED!
Same Logic Applies to RECEIPTS!
Capital Receipts (Owner's Capital, Bank Loan, Sale of Old Van) → Balance Sheet | Revenue Receipts (Sales, Rent/Comm. Earned) → Income Stmt
